quote: I am active duty. Yes. Navy. Four years. Roughly going on five years.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers unprompted detail about his military service length after the rep's simple yes/no question — a small engagement signal. This category (military discount) isn't documented anywhere in the schema's cross-sell or discount catalog, so it's an unschematized gap rather than a specific misapplication.

quote: Alright. I'm sending you a text right now so you can have my number.
stewart_read: Rep gives out a personal number for bill follow-up, matching the anti-pattern the schema flags for privacy/scale review — this is the opposite of trust_building_micro_trades (which describes substituting automation for a personal touch); here the rep substitutes a personal channel for what should be a company process.
coaching_implication: Flag for the floor-wide privacy review noted in the schema's roadmap section; once automated bill capture ships, this rep should be migrated off personal-number workarounds.

quote: Is there anything else that interested you in solar or just getting an estimate to see?
stewart_read: Rep asks the interest question but the customer's flat answer ('Just trying to get an estimate to be honest') is accepted at face value with no follow-up to find a deeper motivator (bill pain, new-move context, etc.), and it is never revisited when booking the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic — the rep may have judged the answer as genuinely thin and not worth pressing on a cooperative, already-moving call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to probe one layer deeper on flat 'just want an estimate' answers, especially with a customer who just moved in — new-homeowner context is itself a usable interest anchor the rep never surfaced.

stewart_read: Bill figure is captured cleanly but the rep immediately pivots to a tangent about meter wiring rather than acknowledging or flipping the number into urgency.
coaching_implication: Point to this as a clean capture-without-flip example — the rep had the number and moved straight to logistics instead of using it as leverage.

quote: We've locked you out for an hour just so you don't feel rushed, and they'll go over, show you the details, estimate, all that.
stewart_read: Rep completes the hour-block element but never explicitly states the appointment will be a phone call versus in-person, nor gets the 'no driving / at your computer' instruction or the 'is that fair?' handshake — an incomplete button-up rather than a customer-stated conditional constraint.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full button-up checklist verbatim — phone-appointment framing, no-driving/computer instruction, and the explicit fairness handshake — since none of the three appear here despite an otherwise smooth close.

stewart_read: Customer seems to momentarily lose the thread of the scheduling question, and the rep doesn't restate or firmly anchor before moving to the next day option, contributing to a slightly bumpy multi-step negotiation to land the final time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive — a minor communication hiccup handled fine in the end (rep did land a locked day/time by 06:10), so this is a small friction point rather than a real gap.
coaching_implication: Minor — no action needed beyond noting the rep recovered fine; not worth spending 1-on-1 time on.
